                    ### Question
                    Which of the following causes of malabsorption occurs with alteration of the intestinal mucosa ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. The Crigler-Najjar syndrome.
opb. A cholestasis
opc. Celiac disease
opd. Achalasia

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Celiac disease is characterized by an immune response to gluten, leading to damage of the intestinal mucosa and resulting in malabsorption of nutrients, which aligns with consensus understanding. In contrast, achalasia is primarily an esophageal motility disorder that does not directly affect the intestinal mucosa, thus it is not a cause of malabsorption related to mucosal alteration. Cholestasis involves bile flow obstruction, impairing fat absorption but does not directly alter the intestinal mucosa. Crigler-Najjar syndrome is a metabolic disorder unrelated to the intestinal mucosa and does not cause malabsorption. Therefore, the only option that causes malabsorption through alteration of the intestinal mucosa is celiac disease.
